text: This closes the capstone and the course. The three confirmed causes from Lesson 24 get fixed, each verified against the same evidence that confirmed it, and the real deliverable -- a genuine prevention plan -- gets built, so this exact pattern doesn't quietly recur the next time some other scoped app grows the same way.

An index was added on the store-region and active fields, matching the list view's real filter -- the query plan now shows an index seek instead of a full table scan, and the list opens about as fast as it did back at 50 stores. The corrected ChecklistUtils function, one query instead of one per item, was deployed, and approval flows clear in a couple of seconds again instead of sitting for a minute. The Nightly Rollup job was moved to 2 AM, clear of the 7 AM submission spike, so the two jobs no longer compete for the same semaphore pool at all.

Stopping at the fix only solves this one instance. The prevention plan sets real alert thresholds: sustained list-view load past 1.5 seconds, semaphore utilization past 80% in any scheduled window, script execution time past twice its rolling average, and -- most important -- an alert tied to usage growth itself, crossing every 100-user milestone, which is the one threshold that would have caught this months before any user complained.

Three pillars make this a repeatable practice instead of a lucky catch: growth-tied monitoring thresholds, a quarterly or growth-milestone review that re-runs these same diagnostic checks by hand, and Automated Test Framework performance regression tests that fail a future build if a change measurably worsens a captured baseline -- the exact guardrail that would have caught the query-in-a-loop at commit time.

This course has been about finding and fixing performance problems after they appear. The query-in-a-loop in ChecklistUtils was never a mistake anyone would have caught reviewing the code in isolation -- it only became a real problem at a scale the original design never accounted for. Next, ServiceNow Technical Architecture is about the design decisions made before a problem like this one ever gets the chance to exist.
